'''Roland Zdeněk Bulirsch''' (10 November 1932 – 21 September 2022) was a German mathematician specialising in [[numerical analysis]]. He studied and taught at the [[Technical University of Munich]], and taught internationally as visiting professor. He was co-author of the reference book ''Introduction to Numerical Analysis'', and president of the edition of the works by [[Johannes Kepler]]. He received honorary doctorates from international universities, and several awards.

== Life and career ==
Bulirsch was born in [[Liberec]] (Reichenberg) on 10 November 1932.<ref name="Bauer">{{cite web |last1 = Bauer|first1 = Friedrich L.|last2 = Bode|first2 = Arndt|url = https://badw.de/fileadmin/pub/akademieAktuell/2007/23/13_Bode_Bauer.pdf|title = Zum 75. Geburtstag von Roland Bulirsch|website = badw.de|date = November 2007|language=de|access-date = 23 September 2022}}</ref> He [[Expulsion of Germans from Czechoslovakia|had to leave Czechoslovakia]] in 1946. In 1947, he became an apprentice as a machinist with [[Siemens-Schuckert]] in Nuremberg, completing in 1951. He achieved the [[Abitur]] in [[Nördlingen]] in 1954,<ref name="Bauer" /> and then studied mathematics and physics at the [[Technical University of Munich]] to 1959,<ref name="TUM">{{cite news|url = http://www-hm.ma.tum.de/archiv/ei1/ws9798/geschichte/t/node49.html|title = Prof. Dr. Dr. h.c. Roland Bulirsch - Ordinarius|publisher = [[Technical University of Munich]]|date = 2022|language=de|access-date = 23 September 2022}}</ref> earning his Ph.D. there in 1961, supervised by [[Klaus Samelson]], and his habilitation in mathematics in 1965.<ref name="Bauer" /> He taught as associated professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]], from 1967 to 1969, and as professor of [[applied mathematics]] at the [[University of Cologne]] from 1969. He joined the faculty in Munich in 1973.<ref name="TUM" />

He was elected a member of the [[Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] in 1991. In 1998 he became president of the edition of the works by [[Johannes Kepler]]. He was emerited in 2001.<ref name="Bauer" />

Bulirsch specialised in [[numerical analysis]].<ref name="Breitner">{{cite book |doi = 10.1007/978-3-540-74238-8_1|title = From Nano to Space|pages = 1–2|date = 2008|isbn = 978-3-540-74237-1|last1 = Breitner|first1 = Michael|last2 = Denk|first2 = Georg|last3 = Rentrop|first3 = Peter| chapter=Roland Bulirsch - 75th Birthday |doi-access = free}}</ref> He is the author (with [[Josef Stoer]]) of ''Introduction to Numerical Analysis'', a standard reference for the theory of [[numerical methods]], and has also authored numerous other books and articles. The book ''From Nano to Space: Applied Mathematics Inspired by Roland Bulirsch'' is a tribute to his work.<ref name="Breitner" /> The [[Bulirsch–Stoer algorithm]] is named after him and Stoer.

Bulirsch received honorary doctorates from the [[University of Hamburg]], the Technical University of Liberec, the National Technical University of Athens and the [[University of Viên Toán Hoc]] in Hanoi. He was awarded a medal from the Union of Czech Mathematicians and Physicists, and a medal from the [[Charles University]] in Prague. In 1998, he received the [[Bavarian Maximilian Order for Science and Art]], and the following year the Liebig-Denkmünze, the highest award of the Heimatkreis Reichenberg. He was elected to the {{ill|Sudetendeutsche Akademie der Wissenschaften und Künste|de}} the same year. In 2012, he received the Großer Sudetendeutscher Kulturpreis.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://reichenberg.de/category/aus-der-sudetendeutschen-landsmannschaft/page/16/|title = Großer Sudetendeutscher Kulturpreis 2012 an Prof. Roland Zdeněk Bulirsch|publisher = Reichenberg|date = 8 May 2012|language=de|access-date = 27 September 2022}}</ref>

=== Personal life ===
Bulirsch and his wife Waltraut had two daughters. She died in 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url = https://trauer.merkur.de/traueranzeige/waltraut-bulirsch|title = Waltraut Bulirsch|type = death notice|publisher = [[Münchner Merkur]]|date = 17 February 2020|language=de|access-date = 22 September 2022}}</ref>

Bulirsch died in [[Gauting]] on 21 September 2022 at age 89.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://bulirsch.eu/curriculum-vitae/|title = Univ.-Prof. em. Dr. rer.nat. Dr. h.c. mult. Roland Zdeněk Bulirsch (Bulíř)|website = bulirsch.eu|date = 21 September 2020|language=de|access-date = 23 September 2022}}</ref>
